claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is compliant because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout is limited and reversible, and the known Spanish-language billing support weakness can be handled through explicit model-card disclosure plus monitoring even though that segment remains exposed and no approved risk acceptance covers it.
decision_criteria: If certification policy requires exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance before launch while the segment remains exposed, the action is noncompliant.

If certification policy permits launch with a disclosed material limitation for the exposed use case, and the disclosure is actually present in the certification record, the action could become compliant_with_caveats.
General monitoring, rollback, and 5% rollout size are not sufficient by themselves under the stated policy text.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model card or certification artifact showing the Spanish-language billing limitation is explicitly disclosed for the launch use case.

Provide the governing certification/release-policy text that states certification may proceed with an unresolved material limitation if it is disclosed, even when the affected segment remains exposed.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout cohort does or does not include Spanish-language billing support traffic in practice.
Provide any reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this exact exposure.
specific_concerns: The policy text expressly says rollout controls, rollback capability, monitoring, and small-cohort launch do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.

The actor summary says the Spanish-language billing support segment remains below target and is still in the initial cohort, so the key policy-safe harbors of exclusion or approved risk acceptance are not satisfied.
No admissible evidence is provided here showing the actual model-card disclosure text, that it was included in the certification packet, or that it is sufficient for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence is provided showing that certification is allowed when a material weakness remains unresolved but disclosed; that predicate is asserted, not demonstrated.
Public guidance from NIST or other sources may support monitoring, but it does not by itself satisfy the stated release-policy condition.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record rather than merely arguable.
That explicit model-card disclosure alone is sufficient to cure the unresolved exposure for certification.
That public AI risk-management guidance materially supports the policy conclusion needed here, as opposed to general monitoring practice.
